analysis:
Examined all supplied tests, entrypoint base/head, Bedrock base/patch and file metadata. No independently supported security regression in this scope. These scanner changes do not modify provider transport encryption, attestation, authorization or inference controls covered by A-001, A-003, TB-002 and TB-011; the supplied canonical index does not define detailed CI billing controls.
.github/scripts/threat-model-review.py:16-23 validates a trusted environment timeout within 60–3000 seconds, preserving the 900-second default; lines 31-43 arm and cancel the alarm and report setup failure without claiming clearance. Existing zero-exit behavior for general exceptions is unchanged.
.github/scripts/threat_review/bedrock.py patch head:46-57 adds workload planning with a bounded 500-call ceiling and higher output allowance. Head:68-88 cumulatively admits scheduled calls plus one repair slot and makes ceiling exhaustion sticky. Base:84-97 shows the retained stop/allowance checks before invocation; base:125-148 counts attempted native calls and restricts fallback to explicit unavailable errors. Accounting failures still stop further requests. Increased paid capacity and 600-second request waits are intentional new resource exposure, not evidence of unbounded spending.
.github/scripts/test-threat-model-review.py:738-775 changes workflow expectations for pinned base context, longer runtime and workload policy; surrounding tests exercise stale snapshots, incomplete retries, credential redaction, comment spoofing and HTTP boundaries. Assertions are not proof that the workflow enforces them.
Integration must inspect the actual workflow and scheduling callers of plan_calls, including source/depth/integration and repair admission, and reconcile durable per-PR/run admission and fallback reservations with the higher native allowance. Confirm the 3000-second alarm leaves publication time inside the actual job deadline and failures cannot produce merge clearance. Those implementations are outside this batch, so these are unresolved contracts rather than findings.
